title: Which policy generated this trajectory?
subtitle: Search-agent RL · Mixed-version rollouts · TRPO
intro: One previously unlisted technical blog from the overlap window; historical reading derives the gap between surrogate improvement and policy improvement.

articles.title: Filtering tasks; tracking the policy behind each token

blocks.text: For search agents, filtering and rollout synchronization jointly determine the update data. This October 22 blog is newly included: eight probes per question, then SFT on 4,932 traces and GRPO on 1,480 tasks.[1]

blocks.label: Independent Bernoulli illustration: intermediate difficulty is more likely retained; not a paper theorem

blocks.text: Eight failures do not establish unlearnability. Filtering depends on both policy and tools; the reported pipeline does not isolate their contributions.[1]

blocks.caption: Blog report; both tools and training changed.[1]

blocks.tex: q(\tau\mid x)=\prod_{t=1}^T q_{v_t}(a_t\mid h_t),\qquad w(\tau)=\prod_{t=1}^T\frac{\pi_\theta(a_t\mid h_t)}{q_{v_t}(a_t\mid h_t)}
blocks.label: Illustration: execution version v_t; exact trajectory IS requires actual behavior probabilities and support

blocks.text: Hot-Load preserves requests and caches across weight changes. Strict on-policy operation can reset prompt caches and wait for all replicas. The equation is not an implemented correction; cached execution need not equal recomputation under new weights.[1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The fastest delta Hot-Load is about 15× the average cold start, measuring weight updates only. No unbiased mixed-version gradient guarantee is established.[1]

blocks.text: Natural policy gradients and conservative policy iteration (2002) motivate TRPO (2015): improving on old data changes future state visitation.[2,3]

blocks.label: Discounted MDP; 0<γ<1; unnormalized occupancy; bounded advantage
Identity and surrogate: replacing new occupancy with old occupancy is the approximation [2]

blocks.text: Coupling bounds history divergence by tα; zero mean under the old policy bounds the new mean advantage by 2εα.[2]

blocks.label: Slightly looser form of Appendix A coupling bound; second-order error [2]

blocks.tex: J(\pi\prime)\ge L_\pi(\pi\prime)-C D_{\rm KL}^{\max}(\pi,\pi\prime),\quad C=\frac{4\epsilon\gamma}{(1-\gamma)^2},\quad D_{\rm KL}^{\max}=\max_s D_{\rm KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid s)\Vert\pi\prime(\cdot\mid s))
blocks.label: Paper KL lower bound; exact improvement over the old-policy baseline guarantees nondecrease [2]

blocks.tex: \max_\theta\ \mathbb E_{s\sim d_\pi,a\sim\pi}\!\left[\frac{\pi_\theta(a\mid s)}{\pi(a\mid s)}A_\pi(s,a)\right]\quad\mathrm{s.t.}\quad\mathbb E_{s\sim d_\pi}D_{\rm KL}(\pi\Vert\pi_\theta)\le\delta,\quad d_\pi=(1-\gamma)\rho_\pi
blocks.label: Practical TRPO: average-KL constraint, approximately solved by conjugate gradients and line search [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Average KL and estimated advantages do not directly inherit monotonicity. Atari used one run per game. Question: can sampled-prefix average KL control rare harmful prefixes in long trajectories?[2]
